To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the hippocampal formation is a crucial part of the navigation system and (2) it represents space by a gain field code of sensory cues.

the hippocampal formation can be understood as a system of multiple maps that are involved in spatial behaviour and that the representation of the environment is not necessarily based on a single place map, but can arise as the result of a combination of multiple sensory-motor maps.
“A direction-invariant representation of the spatial location of a target can be generated by gain-field modulation of a sensory-motor map.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the hippocampus is involved in spatial orientation in the plane and how it is related to the sensory-motor maps in the cortex.
the representation of space and the generation of locomotion in the brain.
the representation of spatial information in the brain and its relation to the sensory-motor systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a direction-invariant representation of the spatial map can be generated from a retinotopic representation of the cues and their gain-field modulation, however, this representation is only approximate and not as accurate as the representation in a place-cell layer.
the model presented here provides a framework to understand how the hippocampus might be used for navigation.
the representation of the space is implicit and not explicit, i.e. the hippocampus is not the “map of the world”, but the “map of navigation” (see also O’Keefe & Burgess 1996).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the representation of space by place cells in the hippocampus is not a representation of the environment as a whole.

the hippocampus might be involved in the representation of the sensory-motorspace, but that the representation is not a place-coding of the environment but rather the representation of the parameters of the sensory-motive maps.
the sensory-motor maps of the brainstem and parietal cortex are the basis of navigation and the hippocampus is involved in the representation of space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the representation of the environment in the hippocampus is not a simple projection of sensory-motor maps but rather the result of the interplay of multiple mechanisms that include the sensory-motor maps and the head direction signal, but also the activity patterns in other brain areas such as the prefrontal cortex and the amygdala.
a representation of the metric of the space is necessary to generate a direction-invariant place representation in the hippocampal system.

the sensory-motor maps in the brainstem, superior colliculus and the parietial cortex are the main source for the representation of spatial information in the hippocampus, which is based on gain-field modulation and the metric of the underlying sensory-motor map.
